teams.heading: Jake White's arrival prompts former Wallabies star to consider Fiji switch
teams.body: A former Wallabies star is reported to be considering a switch to Fiji, a move that follows Jake White's appointment as head coach. White was confirmed at a press conference on Tuesday, having emerged from a field of 31 applicants, and he takes over the 2027 World Cup project from interim Senirusi Seruvakula. The 62-year-old South African's brief is to get Fiji's best-prepared group to Australia, with Pool C opponents Argentina, Canada and Spain already set.

lead.why: A new player-interest story that broke after the White appointment, so it is fresh and not a repeat of the confirmation.

teams.heading: Planet Rugby: Maro Itoje's back-row role could offer Steve Borthwick an option
teams.body: Planet Rugby's round-three England winners and losers column argues that Maro Itoje's move to the back row, where he was named Player of the Match against Bristol Bears, could present Steve Borthwick with a different picture in his back five. The column also floats Alex Coles's switch to the wide forward role for Northampton as a possible idea for November, pointing to 67 metres from 10 carries and a try. George Martin and Ben Bamber are cited as further options for Borthwick.

teams.heading: Stade Français's Yoan Tanga and Noah Nene injured before Bulls clash
teams.body: Stade Français go into Saturday's Champions Cup opener at Loftus Versfeld with two more injury doubts beyond the hooker Lucas Peyresblanques. Yoan Tanga left the 30-22 Top 14 win over Montpellier after nine minutes with a rib injury, and the extent of it remains unclear. Noah Nene was replaced in the 18th minute after hurting his right ankle, and Paul Gustard, the Stade Français coach, indicated he could be sidelined for around two weeks, pending further medical examinations.

lead.why: The only fresh item in the pack, and it is a Stade Français club story, so it is labelled as such; it covers two players other than Lucas Peyresblanques, whose injury was already reported today.

teams.heading: Fergus Slattery, Ireland's 61-cap flanker and 1974 Lion, died aged 77
teams.body: The Telegraph's obituary, published 4 June, marks the death of Fergus Slattery, who was 77. Slattery won 61 caps for Ireland between 1970 and 1984, including 18 as captain, and led the 1979 tour of Australia. He was also in the 1974 British and Irish Lions back row in South Africa, alongside England's Roger Uttley and Wales's Mervyn Davies, a trio the obituary says many still regard as the best Lions back row combination ever. At his retirement his 61 caps were a world record for a flanker.

lead.why: The only men's Ireland item in the pack, and it is dated June, so the body says so plainly.

teams.heading: World Rugby loses bid to have brain injury claims thrown out
teams.body: World Rugby and UK governing bodies lost their bid to have brain injury claims brought by rugby players thrown out of court, a ruling reported on 21 August. Later reports say hundreds of players have won the right for their claims to go to trial. The Guardian reports the claimants now face a £2.8m legal bill to keep the case going, and the case remains open. Italy are not named in any of the coverage I have seen, so the Azzurri's stake is indirect.

teams.heading: Mark Jones insists Tom Rogers was signed as a hybrid back
teams.body: Ospreys head coach Mark Jones has pushed back on the idea that Ospreys back Tom Rogers is a full-back, insisting the 27-year-old was signed as a hybrid back. Rogers started on the right wing against Sharks and Lions before taking the 15 jersey against Dragons and winning man of the match, a run that keeps him in the mix for Wales coach Steve Tandy's squad. Tandy names his squad for the Nations Championship on 20 October.

teams.heading: Shaun Edwards joins Pumas as defence coach until 2027 World Cup
teams.body: Shaun Edwards, the Englishman who left France's defence role earlier this year after helping them win three Six Nations titles, has joined Argentina's coaching staff on a deal running to the end of the 2027 World Cup in Australia, BBC Sport reported on 9 October. Edwards will first fulfil a consultancy with England's women's team before starting with the Pumas at the end of October, alongside Mario Ledesma. "I've always admired the ability and quality of Argentine players," he said.

lead.why: Edwards' appointment is a different story from the Ledesma item already shown, and it reshapes Argentina's defence ahead of the November tests.

teams.heading: Len Ikitau, Hunter Paisami, Jordan Petaia out; Suaalii may return to centre
teams.body: Len Ikitau (concussion), Hunter Paisami (suspension) and Jordan Petaia (ankle) are all ruled out of Saturday's second Bledisloe Cup Test against New Zealand, and Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii could move back into the centres after two games on the wing. Suaalii, who played 24 successive Tests at outside centre before the switch, says he is enjoying the change, telling reporters in Sydney that it is 'a different part of my journey.' The match is at Accor Stadium, where Australia will try to bounce back from the 50-19 Eden Park defeat.

lead.why: New injury and availability news for Saturday's Bledisloe Cup Test, and it directly affects Australia's selection.

teams.heading: Japan Sakura Sevens reclaim Asian Games women's gold; men take bronze
teams.body: The Japan Sakura Sevens reclaimed Asian Games women's gold in Aichi-Nagoya, beating defending champions China 10-5 in a tight final, as reported on 5 October. Japan's men took bronze after a 17-5 win over Korea, having lost a semi-final 10-7 to China, a result seen as an upset. Hong Kong China completed a three-peat of men's titles, winning the final 26-0.

lead.why: It is the strongest Japan story in today's pack, with two outlets covering it, and it is not one of the stories already reported this week.

teams.heading: Jeff Wilson lauds Wallace Sititi's return to form in Bledisloe Cup win
teams.body: All Blacks great Jeff Wilson has singled out Wallace Sititi after the number eight's display in Saturday's 50-19 Bledisloe Cup opener win over Australia at Eden Park. Speaking on The Breakdown, Wilson said Sititi "needed a big game at some point for the All Blacks" after a slow 2026 start. "I thought this was one of his best games in the jersey because the All Blacks needed it and he brought it." Head coach Dave Rennie had publicly admonished Sititi after a poor display against Italy.

lead.why: It is a new item from the pack, it is about a selection storyline (Sititi's form after Rennie's public criticism), and it is not a repeat of the Read quote already reported.

teams.heading: Jake White returns as Fiji head coach, signed through 2027 World Cup
teams.body: Jake White, the former Springboks coach who led the side to Rugby World Cup glory over England in Paris, has signed on to take Fiji through to the 2027 World Cup. Fiji are on their third head coach this year after Mick Byrne parted ways with the union, and Senirusi Seruvakula oversaw defeats to Wales, England and Scotland before losing the Pacific Nations Cup final to Japan. Planet Rugby cites reports that players were unhappy with White's leadership at the Bulls, his most recent professional role.

lead.why: Stormers team news is the same Louw story already on this tab, so the Fiji appointment of a former Springboks coach is the strongest new item with a South Africa angle.
